unblocked_scope.summary: FE-1 through FE-7: new ResolutionScope type/field, engine branch, both call-site signature updates, scope-aware suggestion copy, and regression + integrity tests. Every pairRules entry (live + proposed) ships resolutionScope: 'day' — reproduces today's exact display behavior, zero regression. Ready for qa-lead now.
key_findings_from_planning: Source research (docs/tasks/routine_updates 2.0/CONFLICT_RESOLUTION_SCOPE.md) cites PRD_Spec.md §5.2 / USER_STORIES.md US-09, which are stale pre-ruleset-migration text (parseInciTags, 4-tag matrix) — already flagged stale by vials-conflict-matrix-expansion on 2026-08-04. Not re-fixed here; noted so nobody re-anchors on those sections.

Source research's Phase 12.1 note ('the routine step already carries RoutineStep.period') is factually wrong — RoutineStep has no period field; period comes from the containing Routine.timeOfDay. Engine task is a real signature change, not copy-only.

PairRule already had a scope field ('same_period'|'same_day'|'anywhere') before this task, but it is functionally inert beyond an anywhere-vs-not binary — resolve.ts's findPairViolations treats same_period/same_day identically. The real, already-live AM/PM-splittability signal in the scheduler is whether a rule's resolutions array contains 'separate_periods'. This task's new resolutionScope field deliberately does not touch either of those (Option A, confirmed) — see tech design Assumption 2.

still_blocked.scope: Which pairs reclassify resolutionScope 'day' -> 'slot' (source research §4), and the reactive-skin condition-interaction question (§7). Bounded decision list below — confirm or correct each row, not an open audit.
still_blocked.reviewer_scope_note: Unlike vials-conflict-matrix-expansion's FE-4, this sign-off only changes DISPLAY behavior (whether the Routines-screen warning renders). routineEngine/resolve.ts (auto-scheduling: freeze/split/relocate) is untouched by this task — a 'slot' approval here does not change what the app automatically does to a user's routine, only what warning it shows. If you're used to matrix-expansion's blast-radius warning, this task's stakes are narrower by design (tech design §5).
still_blocked.overlap_note: Some of the same tag-pairs below are ALSO subject to vials-conflict-matrix-expansion's still-open FE-4 (pair existence/severity) and/or proposedPairRules.ts's gate (PROPOSED_V12_PAIR_RULES_ENABLED = false). That is a DIFFERENT question (does the pair exist, at what severity) from this task's question (if it exists, is it slot or day). A pair may need both sign-offs. Per product decision this planning pass, the two decision lists stay separate documents, not merged — flagging the overlap here only for sequencing awareness.

engineer_handoff.summary: FE-1 through FE-7 implemented exactly per the approved plan. FE-1: ResolutionScope = 'slot'|'day' + required PairRule.resolutionScope (rulesetTypes.ts). FE-2: resolutionScope: 'day' on all 7 live actives.json entries + all 4 PROPOSED_V12_PAIR_RULES entries. FE-3: detectConflicts's new period-awareness is backward-compatible, not a hard replacement — steps: ConflictStepInput[] = RoutineStep & { period?: Period } (period optional, so every pre-existing plain-RoutineStep[] caller keeps compiling/behaving identically); a 'slot' rule only suppresses when both matched steps carry a known, differing period, else falls back to firing (matches 'day' behavior — never a silent false negative for callers that haven't adopted tagging). FE-4: both RoutinesScreen.tsx call sites (the conflictMap builder, and the allSteps prop into ConflictWarningInline) now tag am/pm steps with period before merging; ConflictWarningInline's own default path tags morningSteps/eveningSteps internally. FE-5: resolutionScope/period deliberately kept out of the shared ConflictResult/ConflictRule types in src/types/index.ts (display-only per tech design SS1) -- ConflictWarningInline looks the matched PairRule back up by id from ACTIVES_RULESET.pairRules and computes a suggestion override only for a same-period 'slot' hit, via one generic buildSlotScopeSuggestion(period) template. FE-6/FE-7: new engineer-owned unit tests added to the co-located src/utils/conflictEngine.test.ts (fixture 'slot' PairRule via the same jest.mock pattern qa-lead used, plus an unperiod-tagged-fallback-still-warns case) and src/utils/routineEngine/rulesetIntegrity.test.ts (completeness assertion over both actives.json pairRules and PROPOSED_V12_PAIR_RULES, independent of the feature flag).
engineer_handoff.unplanned_deviation: tests/conflict-matrix-expansion/existing-pairs-regression.test.ts (FE-8, qa-lead-owned, from the vials-conflict-matrix-expansion task) asserts each of the 7 live pairRules toEqual a full object literal. Adding the spec-mandated resolutionScope field to all 7 entries necessarily broke that literal equality even though severity/trigger/copy (the property that test's own docstring says it protects) are provably unchanged -- its own second describe block, which checks id+severity via detectConflicts end-to-end, still passes untouched. Added resolutionScope: 'day' to each of the 7 expected literals plus a dated explanatory comment in the file, rather than leaving it red or reverting FE-2. Logged in progress/conflict-resolution-scope.md per architecture-review.md's deviation-handling rule.
